title: Factorial Comparison of Working Memory Models
authors: Ronald van den Berg, Edward Awh, Wei Ji Ma
caption_short: Example trial procedure in delayed estimation of color: subjects view a set of colored items, and after a brief delay report the color of one probed item by clicking on a color wheel.

notes: Cropped from page 3 (journal page 126) of the published APA typeset PDF at 440 dpi; caption text excluded. Figure 2 is the paper's schematic of the delayed-estimation paradigm (memory array -> delay -> continuous report on a color wheel). The delayed-estimation benchmark analysed in this paper pools 10 previously published experiments (Table 1, same page): E1 Wilken & Ma 2004 (color wheel, Caltech); E2 Zhang & Luck 2008 (color wheel, UC Davis); E3 Bays et al. 2009 (color wheel, UCL); E4 Anderson et al. 2011 (orientation 360deg, U Oregon); E5 Anderson & Awh 2012 (orientation 180deg, U Oregon); E6 Anderson & Awh 2012 (orientation 360deg, U Oregon); E7-E9 Van den Berg et al. 2012 (color scrolling, color wheel, orientation 180deg; Baylor); E10 Rademaker et al. 2012 (orientation 180deg, Vanderbilt). Combined: 164 subjects, 131,452 trials. Figure 2 illustrates the color-wheel version; orientation experiments used an analogous continuous report. Data and code: https://github.com/WeiJiMaLab/delayed_estimation_benchmark. The PMC author-manuscript version is PMC4159389 (its PDF is behind a proof-of-work challenge; the Ma lab copy was used instead — note the task brief cited PMC3949221, but Unpaywall/PMC resolve DOI 10.1037/a0035234 to PMC4159389).
